newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says deregulation has helped push down costs.
newsitem.headline: Japan says deregulation has helped push down costs.

text.p: Deregulatory measures introduced since 1990 have helped push down the costs of various services in the Japanese economy, the Economic Planning Agency (EPA) said in a report released on Tuesday.
EPA said the "users' merit" from the deregulation steps amounted to an annual average of 4.62 trillion yen, or 0.98 percent of the nominal gross domestic product (GDP).

The "users' merit" shows how much users benefitted from the fall in costs brought about by the deregulation. The figure is obtained by multiplying the margin of decrease in costs of the services by the demand in those services, the EPA said.
The agency also said in theoretical terms, the decline in costs should have lowered consumer prices by 1.14 percent.
